title: Affine-local criterion for geometric irreducibility on an irreducible scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ an irreducible $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if, for every nonempty affine open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ [def-pc-scheme], the affine $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the $k$-algebra structure induced from $X$, is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Moreover, if $X$ is geometrically irreducible, every nonempty open subscheme of $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. No reducedness, quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038G, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-local, equivalence (1) and (2), restricted to irreducible X, and final assertion, lines 1405--1442

proof.text: Assume first that X is geometrically irreducible and let K/k be a field extension, so that X_K is irreducible. The projection X_K -> X is surjective: it is the base change of Spec K -> Spec k along the structure morphism of X, Spec K -> Spec k is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective], and surjectivity is stable under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. If U is a nonempty affine open of X, then U_K = U x_k Spec K is the open subscheme of X_K given by the preimage of U (fibre product with an open subscheme), and it is nonempty because U is nonempty and X_K -> X is surjective. A nonempty open of the irreducible space X_K is irreducible, so U_K is irreducible. The affine identification U = Spec Gamma(U,O_X) is an isomorphism of k-schemes for the induced k-algebra structure, so (Spec Gamma(U,O_X))_K is isomorphic to U_K and is irreducible for every K/k; by the definition this is the geometric irreducibility of Spec Gamma(U,O_X). The same argument applied to any nonempty open V of X proves the moreover clause: V_K is a nonempty open of the irreducible scheme X_K, hence irreducible, for every K/k.

source.place: Tag 038G, proof of lemma-geometrically-irreducible-local, the sentence identifying affine schemes with their coordinate algebras and the implications (1) implies (2) and the final assertion, lines 1430--1438

proof.text: Conversely, suppose every nonempty affine open U of X has Spec Gamma(U,O_X) geometrically irreducible over k. Take the family of all nonempty affine open subschemes of X; it covers X because affine opens form a basis of a scheme, and it is nonempty because X is irreducible, hence nonempty. For a field extension K/k the preimages U_K of these opens under the projection X_K -> X form an open covering of X_K. The identification U = Spec Gamma(U,O_X) of k-schemes gives U_K = Spec(Gamma(U,O_X) tensor_k K), so every U_K is irreducible by the hypothesis. Since X is irreducible, any two nonempty opens U and V meet; the projection X_K -> X is surjective, by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] as in step 1, so the preimage (U cap V)_K = U_K cap V_K is nonempty. Thus the base-changed covering consists of pairwise intersecting irreducible opens, indexed by a nonempty family.

source.place: Tag 038G, proof of lemma-geometrically-irreducible-local, implications (2) implies (3) and (3) supplies the affine open cover, lines 1434--1438

proof.text: A space covered by a nonempty family of irreducible opens U_i that pairwise intersect is irreducible. It is nonempty since some U_i is. If it is the union of two closed sets Z_1 and Z_2, each irreducible U_i lies in Z_1 or in Z_2; say U_i lies in Z_1. For any j, U_i cap U_j is a nonempty open of the irreducible space U_j, hence dense in U_j, and it lies in the closed set Z_1, so U_j lies in Z_1; hence the whole space is Z_1. (Mathlib states this as PreirreducibleSpace.of_isOpenCover, Mathlib/Topology/Sets/OpenCover.lean:123.) Applied to the covering of X_K from step 2, X_K is irreducible. This holds for every field extension K/k, so X is geometrically irreducible by the definition.
